findings.claim: WP-SCP-020 §4 020B criterion (xi) still reads 'Commit status context = scp/policy-check' unconditionally. The implementation correctly documents that the actual GitHub check context is '{calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check' (workflow lines 43-44), but the parent plan text remains technically inaccurate. An implementor reading only the plan spec for 020D2 branch-protection configuration will receive wrong information.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B: '(xi) Commit status context = `scp/policy-check` (stable; WP-SCP-023 aggregator consumer).' .github/workflows/policy-check.yml lines 43-44: '# GitHub records reusable-workflow checks as "{calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check". / # 020D1/020D2 must verify the combined context before configuring branch protection.' docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020b/dispatch-package.json notes field: 'Reusable-workflow check context records as {calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check and must be verified empirically before 020D2 branch protection is configured.' The workflow and dispatch-package correctly qualify the context; the governing spec (WP-SCP-020 §4 xi) does not.
findings.impact: An implementor reading WP-SCP-020 §4 criterion (xi) as the authoritative spec for 020D2 configuration may hardcode 'scp/policy-check' as the required-status-check context without performing the 020E.a empirical verification. If the 020D1 caller job name is not aligned with the convention, the required check will be permanently unsatisfied and the entire enforcement model will silently fail. The workflow comment mitigates this for readers who inspect the workflow file, but the plan governs the 020D2 dispatch-package instruction.
findings.mitigation: Amend WP-SCP-020 §4 020B criterion (xi) to: 'Commit status context for this job (callee name) is scp/policy-check; the full GitHub check context is {calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check where calling-job-name is determined by the 020D1 caller wrapper. 020D2 must use the empirically verified combined string from 020E.a canary evidence before configuring branch protection.' Amendment is outside 020B scope_boundary; file as a follow-up note in the 020D2 dispatch-package instruction or as an in-line plan amendment in the next plan-touching slice. Tracked-forward: 020D2 dispatch-package must cite the verified combined context string.

findings.claim: The bypass gate (policy-check.yml lines 237-250) selects only the FIRST deny finding's rule_id for the break-glass pairing check. If multiple deny findings are present and scp_bypass=true, subsequent deny findings remain effective and the workflow fails even after a valid bypass pairing passes. This single-bypass-per-invocation behaviour is not documented in the workflow, dispatch-package notes, or any tracked-forward item for ADOPT-001 §12.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 244-250: 'for finding in payload: if finding.get("verdict") == "deny" and finding.get("rule_id"): print(finding["rule_id"]); raise SystemExit(0)'. The raise SystemExit(0) exits after the first deny match. Lines 340-343: 'effective_denies = [item for item in denies if not (bypass_approved and bypass_rule_id and item.get("rule_id") == bypass_rule_id)]' — filters only the single SCP_BYPASS_RULE_ID. WP-SCP-020 §4 020B (viii-c) references 'a matching waivers.json entry' (singular), consistent with the design intent, but does not state the 'first deny found' selection rule. ADOPT-001 §12 (deferred to 020H part 3) will be the primary adopter reference for the three-gate model; the single-bypass limitation must be captured there.
findings.impact: An adopter with two concurrent deny findings (e.g., SCP-R-001 and SCP-R-003 both firing on a PR) who sets scp_bypass=true and provides a waivers.json entry for SCP-R-001 will observe: bypass gate 2 and gate 3 pass for SCP-R-001; the workflow still fails because SCP-R-003 remains in effective_denies. Without documentation of the single-bypass-per-invocation model, this will be diagnosed as a workflow bug. The confusion is compounded by the SCP-E004 annotation reporting bypass active 'until {expires_at}' while the overall check still fails.
findings.mitigation: Add a workflow comment after line 250: '# Bypass covers only the first deny finding; PRs with multiple concurrent deny findings require each rule to be addressed independently or sequentially.' Add a tracked-forward note in the dispatch-package for 020H part 3 requiring ADOPT-001 §12 to document the single-bypass model explicitly. The workflow comment can land in a subsequent fix-round; the 020H part 3 note is a documentation dependency already flagged as deferred.

findings.claim: The new verify_command #6 (bypass-schema round-trip test) validates the rule_id shape (shape 1) acceptance and the empty-rule-id rejection case, but does not test the finding_id shape (shape 2 of waivers-file.schema.json). A regression in shape 2 (e.g., making waiver_id optional when it should be required) would not be caught by verify_commands.

No test case for shape 2: [{'waiver_id':'W-001','finding_id':'F-001','reason':'test','approved_by':'@jrnb2024','created_at':'2026-04-28T00:00:00Z','expires_at':'2099-01-01'}]. schemas/waivers-file.schema.json defines two anyOf shapes; the bypass gate only exercises shape 1 at runtime, but both shapes will be consumed in 020C.1 waiver-aware Rego.
